analogy_candidates.breaks_where: Real balls collide; model assumes independence for CLT math

common_misconceptions: Goal is accurate physics of pegs
CLT says any single ball is predictable
core_claim: Sums of many independent ±1 choices look Gaussian as rows grow

key_concepts.definition_1line: Board of peg rows where ball goes left/right 50-50
key_concepts.name: Galton board

key_concepts.definition_1line: Shorthand for random process + numeric outcome
key_concepts.name: Random variable x
key_concepts.why_matters: Lets us talk about sums, not just balls

key_concepts.definition_1line: Sum of n hops; distribution -> bell as n grows
key_concepts.name: Central limit theorem (preview)
key_concepts.why_matters: Explains why normal shows up for heights, prime factors, etc.

mechanism_steps: 5 rows -> final position = sum of 5 hops
Many ghost balls -> bucket counts ~= probabilities
More rows -> histogram looks more like bell curve
narration_beats_3b1b_style: Hook: chaotic one ball, precise many balls
Intuition: idealized ±1 walk, 5 rows, label buckets by sum
Formalize: random variable x late, promise proof + pi formula later
topic: Galton board as Central Limit Theorem preview
